runtime.progress_trace_limit: Snapshots never acquire the COM gate. V6 samples ordinary calls every 256 entries; critical calls and failures retain detailed state. Totals describe the last sampled completion and idle is not proof that another unsampled call is idle. Missing snapshots may mean scheduling/I/O delay or lost queued output. These are not GPU timings.
runtime.gate_waiters_limit: Instantaneous counts without wait-duration attribution; they do not quantify contention cost or prove a deadlock.

limits: These memory counters are logged at startup, before game rendering; they do not show gameplay memory pressure or bandwidth.

The startup process-level free field is 37675008 bytes, while heap_available is 3245286784 bytes in the separate heap accounting. The small process-level free number alone does not establish allocation exhaustion.
Cumulative map_copy_bytes is transferred data over many frames, not live RAM or VRAM allocation.
No device-loss or bridge-failure event was supplied. Absence of these events does not certify long-session memory behavior.

conclusions: The runtime reports v7 native ARM64 selection and both v7 optimization markers, with 1280x720 FIFO and LSFG OFF; the user reports average 20, peak 25 and crowded-running lows around 13 FPS.

The last five 600-interval Present windows are 18.5249, 18.3597, 18.9259, 17.0477 and 23.6424 FPS. Their elapsed-time-weighted rate is 19.0664 FPS; the log does not identify scenes or camera positions.

Across the last two sampled completion counters, each Present corresponds to about 7022 bridge calls, 1067 draws and 9 MiB of shadow Map copies. This is workload evidence, not a measured bottleneck attribution.
Crowded-view slowdown remains consistent with more scene work in game simulation, draw/submission or GPU rendering. No CPU/GPU timing breakdown in this capture selects one cause.
Startup memory statistics cannot support a claim that gameplay has run out of RAM, and the cumulative Map-copy total is not a live-memory allocation.

No native bridge unsupported/fault or device-loss event was captured. The tail still has live interface slots and two maps; without a shutdown report this does not establish either a leak or clean teardown.
The renderer repeats an unknown-interface warning for 0ec870a6-5d7e-4c22-8cfc-5baae07616ed; the warning alone does not identify a performance cause.
The supplied COM files are byte-identical v3 PASS evidence and do not validate the v7 sampler/DSV self-test on hardware.

This observation can guide further rendering-cost reductions while keeping 720p. It cannot quantify a controlled v7-versus-v6 improvement because scene, camera, clocks and cache state were not matched.
